chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: 'May I be your ransom, is there for the Muslims an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said: 'Yes, O Hasan, the greatest and most noble of them.' I said to him: 'And which day is it?' He said: 'The day when the Commander of the Faithful was set up as a standard for the people.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, and which day is it?' He said: 'Indeed, the days revolve, and it is the eighteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, and what should we do in it?' He said: 'Fast it, O Hasan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family, and declare yourself free from those who wronged them and denied their rights, for the Prophets used to command the Successors that the day on which the Successor was appointed should be taken as an Eid.'

I said: 'What is the reward for one of us who fasts it?' He said: 'Fasting for sixty months.' And do not neglect fasting the day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day in which Prophethood was revealed upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like that of sixty months for you.

key_terms.تَتَبَرَّأُ: To declare free from / to disavail
key_terms.ذِی الْحِجَّهِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.عِیدٌ غَیْرُ الْعِیدَیْنِ: An Eid other than the two traditional Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance and reward of fasting on the eighteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) designates the 18th of Dhu al-Hijjah as the 'Greatest and Most Noble' Eid, marking the establishment of Imam Ali (AS) as the public standard of authority. The text prescribes fasting on this day as expiation for sixty months, while also highlighting the 27th of Rajab as the day of the Prophet's initial revelation, which carries an equal reward. This underscores the Shia tradition of commemorating key events in the Imams' lives not just as historical milestones, but as occasions for spiritual purification and increased devotion.
